newsitem.title: INDONESIA: German, Indonesian leaders hold formal talks.
newsitem.headline: German, Indonesian leaders hold formal talks.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Indonesian President Suharto held talks centering on trade and economic cooperation on Monday after a relaxed day of fishing in the Java Sea north of Jakarta.
Guns at Suharto's Merdeka (Freedom) Palace boomed a formal welcome to Kohl under overcast skies and a light rain.
Kohl arrived in Jakarta on Saturday and immediately flew by helicopter to Bira island, Suharto's private enclave among the Thousand Islands near Jakarta.
The two leaders, who last met in mid-July when Suharto underwent medical checks in Germany, spent Sunday fishing and talking.
Officials said the focus of the visit was trade and economic cooperation. But a German official said last week that Kohl was expected to raise human rights concerns during their talks.
Also, German Economic Minister Guenter Rexrodt discussed Indonesia's national car policy with Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie at the weekend, German sources said.
They said Rexrodt told Habibie that Germany could not accept what he described as unfair treatment resulting from the national car policy.

Indonesia earlier this year gave tax and tariff breaks to a company owned Suharto's youngest son to produce a national car in cooperation with a South Korean firm. Japan, the European Union and the United States have complained to the World Trade Organisation over the policy.
Germany and Indonesia are due to sign joint-venture contracts worth 600 million marks ($395 million) and 450 million marks ($296 million) during Kohl's visit.
Khol was to leave for Manila on Tuesday and then continue on to Japan.
